naslov: The Value of Helping a Muslim Brother

segmenti.tekst: [Arabic recitation]

لينذر من كان حيا ويحق القول على الكافرين، صلى الله تعالى عليه وعلى آله الطيبين الطاهرين وأصحابه الكرام الهداة المهتدين وسلم تسليما كثيرا إلى يوم الدين. قال الله في كتابه الكريم: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله حق تقاته ولا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون. أما بعد. Praise belongs to the One, Exalted Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala (glorified and exalted is He), Lord of all the worlds, Lord of the Day of Judgment.

May blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), upon his family, upon his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.

Dear brothers, respected congregation, this religion of ours, Islam, our perfect religion, which Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, delivered to us through His Messenger, came to make things easier for people, not harder.

It came, dear brothers, to bring the hearts of the believers closer through iman (faith), through belief in Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, as is indicated by numerous hadiths of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, among them the hadith narrated by Abu Hurayrah, radiyallahu ta'ala anhu (may Allah be pleased with him), in which the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says… Listen carefully to this hadith, this magnificent, magnificent hadith of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.

The Prophet says: “Man naffasa 'an mu'minin kurbatan min kurab ad-dunya naffasallahu 'anhu kurbatan min kurabi yawm al-qiyamah” – whoever relieves his Muslim brother, a believer, of some hardship of this world, Allah will relieve him of one of the hardships of the Day of Resurrection.

So we see, dear brothers, how the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, encourages us to help our Muslim brother. So if we relieve some hardship of our Muslim brother, and we are able to do it, we are able to do it –

such as helping him in illness, helping him in poverty, helping him in other worldly matters, when someone threatens him, and so on, and so forth, when someone attacks his family, takes his property, and so on – then it is up to a person to help his brother.

What is the reward? The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: Allah will relieve him of one of the hardships on the Day of Judgment. And on the Day of Judgment there are many hardships: on the day when a man will flee from his brother, and from his mother, and from his father, and from his wife, and from his children. So on that day Allah will relieve him, relieve him of some hardship.

The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: “Man yassara 'ala mu'sirin yassarallahu 'alayhi fid-dunya wal-akhirah.” He says: whoever makes things easier for an indebted Muslim brother, Allah will make things easier for him both in this world and in the Hereafter.

Imagine, dear brothers: Allah will make things easier for him both in this world and in the Hereafter. There are many of us, dear brothers, who can help our brothers. A believer must not look at his brother who prays with him in the same row, together they fall into prostration before Allah – look at him while he is in distress, in debt.

It does not befit a believer, a mu'min, when the time of a wedding or music comes, to give 500, a thousand euros each time, so that people see he has given, while meanwhile perhaps his maternal aunt, his paternal aunt, his cousin, and so on, do not have enough for bread.

That is sad. So we ourselves see what the reward is for the one who makes things easier for his Muslim brother. How many times has it happened – surely some of you have felt it – that when someone helps his Muslim brother, Allah compensates him much, much more.

And he does not know where his sustenance comes from, where his provision comes from. That is, dear brothers… The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says further – a very important point – he says: whoever covers the shame, the sin of his Muslim brother, Allah will cover his shame and his sin both in this world and in the Hereafter.
That is why, when a person sees his Muslim brother committing some sin that no one knows about, let him not rush out immediately and say: “Look what he's doing, he did such and such…”

Let him remember these words of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, let him cover the shame of his Muslim brother, so that Allah will cover his shame, his sin, both in this world and in the Hereafter. And how Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, rewards!

And there is no human being who does not sin, who does not commit a major sin. There is no such human being. And whoever mocks his Muslim brother for committing some sin, it is said, will not pass away until Allah tests him with the same sin.

He will not pass away until Allah tests him with the same sin. That is why a person should not hurry to expose his Muslim brother in committing a certain sin; rather, he should advise him. But not in front of everyone; rather, he should take him aside nicely and advise him.

Here we are not talking about people who sin publicly: a man drinks alcohol, takes a selfie, and it's on Instagram, on Facebook. We are not talking about those people. Their story is separate. They expose themselves, no one needs to expose them. Here we are talking about believers who commit some sin that no one else knows about. And sometimes it happens that one of the Muslim brothers sees what he is doing, and then it is up to the person, up to the person, to conceal that shame, that sin of his Muslim brother, so that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, will conceal his shame

and his, and his sin. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says – the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, as he rounds off a chapter that we have spoken about – he says: “Indeed, Allah will be in the aid of His servant as long as the servant is in the aid of his brother.”
As long as we are helping, as long as we help our brother, a believer, a Muslim, in any way – with advice, with money, in any way – Allah will be in our aid.

That is, Allah will help us and will aid us both in this world and in the Hereafter. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says further: “Man salaka tariqan yaltamisu fihi 'ilman sahhalallahu lahu bihi tariqan ilal-jannah.”

Whoever follows a path in pursuit of knowledge, Allah will make easy for him the path to Jannah (Paradise). We spoke about this in previous hutbas (Friday sermons). One of the causes of entering Jannah is that a person seeks knowledge, Shari'ah knowledge, so that he knows how to worship Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.

Believe me, many of our congregation do not know how to perform wudu (ablution) correctly. They do not know how to perform wudu correctly. They do not know how to recite certain surahs correctly, they do not know how to recite Al-Fatihah correctly, and so on, and so forth.

In order for a person… A believer, a Muslim, should make an effort to learn the letters, so that he does not have to worry whether his prayer is valid or invalid. There are many possibilities today. A person can sit at home, on the phone, on a laptop, a tablet, open it and nicely learn the letters, without going anywhere.

He can easily learn the basics of the religion. He sits at home – not to mention how many lectures we have. There is not a day when some lecture on the basics of the religion is not held in some mosque here in Pazar.
For a person to enjoy it: you sit for an hour, and that's it. Also, the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says further: “Ma ijtama'a qawmun fi baytin min buyutillah” –
he says: people will not gather in one of Allah's mosques, houses – “yatluna kitaballahi wa yatadarasunahu baynahum” – reciting and studying the Qur'an – “illa nazalat 'alayhim as-sakinah” –

without, he says, tranquility descending upon them – “wa ghashiyathum ar-rahmah” – and Allah's mercy will cover them – “wa haffathum al-mala'ikah” – and, he says, the angels will surround them with their wings, so that Satan cannot reach them.

And the most important thing, he says: “وَذَكَرَهُمُ اللَّهُ فِيمَنْ عِنْدَهُ” – and he says: Allah will mention them among those who are with Him. Allah will mention them among the angels. Imagine, dear brothers, the honor: that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, mentions your name among the angels,

above the seven heavens, above the Throne. That Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, mentions your name – what an honor that is! But that honor cannot be attained except by the one who recites and studies the Qur'an for the sake of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.

And the last thing that the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, mentions, he says: whoever is held back by his deeds in this world – that is, if his deeds are deficient and he has not done many good deeds by which to enter Jannah – he says, his lineage will not, will not help him on the Day of Judgment.
On the Day of Judgment, dear brothers, our roots will not help us. Our position will not help us, nor children, nor money. “Yawma la yanfa'u malun wa la banun” –
on the day when neither children nor money will benefit, will benefit – “illa man atallaha bi qalbin salim” – except the one who comes before Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, with a pure heart.
I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to make us among these sincere servants of His, who will help their Muslim brother, who will love their Muslim brother, who will respect their Muslim brother.

Because truly, dear brothers, if a person does not apply what we say and what he hears here in these hutbas, then he is ruined, believe me. I mean, I don't know the purpose of his coming to Jumu'ah, I don't know the purpose of his coming to the hutbas.

Because these are the basics, the basics of the religion, basic things that a person needs, needs to know. What can we imams do? We can convey. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, did not come to convince people, nor does any imam, nor any of you who call to Allah's religion.

It is not your duty, nor mine, to convince people; rather, ours is – what? To convey. What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say: “Upon you is only to convey.” It is not upon you to convince people, upon you is to convey. “So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve.” There is no problem at all. “Wa 'alayna al-hisab” – and upon Us is the reckoning. [unclear]

Near, near is the day [unclear] – for some today, for some tomorrow – the angel of death will come, and [unclear] before Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. Alhamdulillahi hamdan kamilan, was-salatu was-salamu 'ala nabiyyina Muhammadin wa 'ala alihi wa sahbihi ajma'in, ta'ziman li nabiyyihi wa takriman li fakhamati sha'nihi [unclear]. قال عز وجل من قائل مخبرا وآمرا: إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي يا أيها الذين آمنوا صلوا عليه وسلموا تسليما. اللهم بارك على محمد وعلى آل محمد كما باركت على إبراهيم وعلى آل إبراهيم
إنك حميد مجيد.
